title: MATH GAOKAO - 145
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a product of sine and cosine using the product-to-sum identity.
questions.question:
Evaluate
\[
\sin 75^\circ \cos 15^\circ.
\]
questions.explanation:
Use the product-to-sum identity
\[
\sin A\cos B=\frac12[\sin(A+B)+\sin(A-B)].
\]
Let \(A=75^\circ\) and \(B=15^\circ\). Then
\[
\sin 75^\circ\cos 15^\circ
=\frac12[\sin(75^\circ+15^\circ)+\sin(75^\circ-15^\circ)].
\]
Thus
\[
\sin 75^\circ\cos 15^\circ
=\frac12[\sin 90^\circ+\sin 60^\circ]
=\frac12\left[1+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right]
=\frac{2+\sqrt3}{4}.
\]
Therefore, the value is \(\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{4}\).

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a product of two cosine functions using the product-to-sum identity.
questions.question:
Evaluate
\[
\cos 75^\circ \cos 15^\circ.
\]
questions.explanation:
Use the product-to-sum identity
\[
\cos A\cos B=\frac12[\cos(A+B)+\cos(A-B)].
\]
Let \(A=75^\circ\) and \(B=15^\circ\). Then
\[
\cos 75^\circ\cos 15^\circ
=\frac12[\cos(75^\circ+15^\circ)+\cos(75^\circ-15^\circ)].
\]
Thus
\[
\cos 75^\circ\cos 15^\circ
=\frac12[\cos 90^\circ+\cos 60^\circ]
=\frac12\left[0+\frac12\right]
=\frac14.
\]
Therefore, the value is \(\frac14\).

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a product of two sine functions using the product-to-sum identity.
questions.question:
Evaluate
\[
\sin 75^\circ \sin 15^\circ.
\]
questions.explanation:
Use the product-to-sum identity
\[
\sin A\sin B=\frac12[\cos(A-B)-\cos(A+B)].
\]
Let \(A=75^\circ\) and \(B=15^\circ\). Then
\[
\sin 75^\circ\sin 15^\circ
=\frac12[\cos(75^\circ-15^\circ)-\cos(75^\circ+15^\circ)].
\]
Thus
\[
\sin 75^\circ\sin 15^\circ
=\frac12[\cos 60^\circ-\cos 90^\circ]
=\frac12\left[\frac12-0\right]
=\frac14.
\]
Therefore, the value is \(\frac14\).

questions.learningObjective: Express a product of sine and cosine as a sum of sine functions.
questions.question:
Express
\[
\sin 3x \cos 2x
\]
as a sum.
questions.explanation:
Use the product-to-sum identity
\[
\sin A\cos B=\frac12[\sin(A+B)+\sin(A-B)].
\]
Let \(A=3x\) and \(B=2x\). Then
\[
\sin 3x\cos 2x
=\frac12[\sin(3x+2x)+\sin(3x-2x)]
=\frac12(\sin 5x+\sin x).
\]
Therefore, the expression is \(\frac12(\sin 5x+\sin x)\).

questions.learningObjective: Express a product of cosine and sine as a difference of sine functions.
questions.question:
Express
\[
\cos 4x \sin 2x
\]
as a sum or difference.
questions.explanation:
Use the product-to-sum identity
\[
\cos A\sin B=\frac12[\sin(A+B)-\sin(A-B)].
\]
Let \(A=4x\) and \(B=2x\). Then
\[
\cos 4x\sin 2x
=\frac12[\sin(4x+2x)-\sin(4x-2x)]
=\frac12(\sin 6x-\sin 2x).
\]
Therefore, the expression is \(\frac12(\sin 6x-\sin 2x)\).

questions.learningObjective: Express a product of two cosine functions as a sum of cosine functions.
questions.question:
Express
\[
\cos 5x \cos 2x
\]
as a sum.
questions.explanation:
Use the product-to-sum identity
\[
\cos A\cos B=\frac12[\cos(A+B)+\cos(A-B)].
\]
Let \(A=5x\) and \(B=2x\). Then
\[
\cos 5x\cos 2x
=\frac12[\cos(5x+2x)+\cos(5x-2x)]
=\frac12(\cos 7x+\cos 3x).
\]
Therefore, the expression is \(\frac12(\cos 7x+\cos 3x)\).

questions.learningObjective: Express a product of two sine functions as a difference of cosine functions.
questions.question:
Express
\[
\sin 6x \sin 2x
\]
as a difference.
questions.explanation:
Use the product-to-sum identity
\[
\sin A\sin B=\frac12[\cos(A-B)-\cos(A+B)].
\]
Let \(A=6x\) and \(B=2x\). Then
\[
\sin 6x\sin 2x
=\frac12[\cos(6x-2x)-\cos(6x+2x)]
=\frac12(\cos 4x-\cos 8x).
\]
Therefore, the expression is \(\frac12(\cos 4x-\cos 8x)\).

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a product of two sine functions using the product-to-sum identity.
questions.question:
Evaluate
\[
\sin 105^\circ \sin 15^\circ.
\]
questions.explanation:
Use the product-to-sum identity
\[
\sin A\sin B=\frac12[\cos(A-B)-\cos(A+B)].
\]
Let \(A=105^\circ\) and \(B=15^\circ\). Then
\[
\sin 105^\circ\sin 15^\circ
=\frac12[\cos(105^\circ-15^\circ)-\cos(105^\circ+15^\circ)].
\]
Thus
\[
\sin 105^\circ\sin 15^\circ
=\frac12[\cos 90^\circ-\cos 120^\circ]
=\frac12\left[0-\left(-\frac12\right)\right]
=\frac14.
\]
Therefore, the value is \(\frac14\).

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a product of two cosine functions using the product-to-sum identity.
questions.question:
Evaluate
\[
\cos 105^\circ \cos 15^\circ.
\]
questions.explanation:
Use the product-to-sum identity
\[
\cos A\cos B=\frac12[\cos(A+B)+\cos(A-B)].
\]
Let \(A=105^\circ\) and \(B=15^\circ\). Then
\[
\cos 105^\circ\cos 15^\circ
=\frac12[\cos(105^\circ+15^\circ)+\cos(105^\circ-15^\circ)].
\]
Thus
\[
\cos 105^\circ\cos 15^\circ
=\frac12[\cos 120^\circ+\cos 90^\circ]
=\frac12\left[-\frac12+0\right]
=-\frac14.
\]
Therefore, the value is \(-\frac14\).

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a product of sine and cosine using the product-to-sum identity.
questions.question:
Evaluate
\[
\sin 75^\circ \cos 45^\circ.
\]
questions.explanation:
Use the product-to-sum identity
\[
\sin A\cos B=\frac12[\sin(A+B)+\sin(A-B)].
\]
Let \(A=75^\circ\) and \(B=45^\circ\). Then
\[
\sin 75^\circ\cos 45^\circ
=\frac12[\sin(75^\circ+45^\circ)+\sin(75^\circ-45^\circ)].
\]
Thus
\[
\sin 75^\circ\cos 45^\circ
=\frac12[\sin 120^\circ+\sin 30^\circ]
=\frac12\left[\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+\frac12\right]
=\frac{\sqrt3+1}{4}.
\]
Therefore, the value is \(\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{4}\).
